basis: Isolated neck extensor myopathy causes persistent weakness of skeletal muscle.
Centronuclear skeletal myopathy; ophthalmoplegia in 25% and respiratory insufficiency in 20% do not meet the involvement threshold.
Craniosynostosis, skeletal abnormalities, intellectual disability and cardiac anomalies define SGS; strabismus and ptosis occur in 30–79%.
Acute malignant myeloid blast proliferation in bone marrow and blood; no additional organ damage established as common.
Lysosomal storage disease with progressive neurodegeneration; retinal degeneration and visual loss affect most patients over the typical course.
Nephrolithiasis is a defining component, reported in 3/3 assessed patients; reproductive obstruction has no axis.
Severe factor IX deficiency; recurrent joint bleeding causes chronic haemophilic arthropathy in well over 30% over the typical untreated course.
Tumour originates in the uterine corpus, a reproductive organ outside the axes; neuroectodermal histology does not establish nervous-system involvement.
Primary immunodeficiency defined by neutrophil dysfunction and leukocytosis; associated abscesses and infections are separately diagnosed diseases.
Congenital cerebellar disorder; functional ocular abnormalities include strabismus in 3/3 and ptosis in 4/4 assessed patients. Renal hypoplasia is not established as common.
Inherited carbohydrate metabolism disorders; liver, eye and neurologic damage vary substantially among subtypes and are not shared across the umbrella.
Inflammation of Tenon's capsule, an ocular supporting structure; an infectious or autoimmune cause is not specified.
Primary dystonia is a neurologic movement disorder; abnormal muscle contractions do not establish primary muscle damage.
Purine metabolism disorder with esophageal atresia in 2/2 and choanal obstruction in at least 1/2; skeletal malformations, including hemivertebrae and clubfoot, occur in 1/2.
Defined by meningeal herniation through a posterior vertebral closure defect; spinal cord function is generally preserved and other complications are occasional.
Malignant tumour arising from the inferior vena cava wall; smooth-muscle histology does not imply skeletal-muscle disease.
Bilateral congenital duplication of formed postaxial digits is a skeletal malformation.
Isolated familial dilated cardiomyopathy; respiratory distress reflects cardiac failure, and SDHA causation alone does not establish systemic metabolic disease.
Spotted-fever rickettsiae infect vascular endothelium and cause small-vessel vasculitis; transient rash does not establish lasting skin damage.
Primary biliary cholangitis is autoimmune destruction of intrahepatic bile ducts; associated extrahepatic autoimmune diseases are separate conditions.
Neurodevelopmental disorder with developmental and speech delay, intellectual disability, microcephaly and structural or white-matter brain abnormalities.
Meningeal tumour of the central nervous system; rhabdoid morphology does not imply skeletal-muscle origin.
Acquired loss of pituitary hormone production defines an endocrine-gland disorder; other organ damage is not intrinsic across the group.
Clonal blood-cell disorder producing monoclonal immunoglobulin; attributable end-organ damage is absent by definition, and malignant progression is a later risk.
The supplied definition specifies erythroblastosis fetalis, an alloimmune red-cell disorder presenting chiefly as neonatal anemia.
